title: About GSFC University
content: GSFC University is located in Vadodara, Gujarat. It was established under the Gujarat Private Universities Act, 2009 by the GSFC Education Society, an initiative of Gujarat State Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd, an industrial group over six decades old. The university is ISO 9001:2015 certified. Its vision is societal development through relevant and cutting-edge knowledge in frontier areas of professional growth.

title: University address and contact details
content: GSFC University, Vigyan Bhavan, P. O. Fertilizernagar, Vadodara - 391750, Gujarat, India. Phone: 0265-3093740 or 07573002444. Admission email: admission@gsfcuniversity.ac.in. WhatsApp: +91 7573002444. A full contact directory PDF is published under the Academics menu of the website.

title: Schools at GSFC University
content: The university has five schools: School of Information & Communication Technology (SoICT), School of Chemical Engineering & Fire Safety (SoCEFS), School of Chemical & Industrial Sciences (SoCIS), School of Life Sciences (SoLS), and School of Management & Entrepreneurship (SoM&E).

title: Programs in the School of Information & Communication Technology
content: The School of ICT (SoICT) offers: B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering, B.Tech. Electronics and Communication Engineering, Bachelor in Computer Application (BCA), M.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering, and Ph.D. Computer Science and Engineering.

title: Programs in the School of Chemical Engineering & Fire Safety
content: The School of Chemical Engineering & Fire Safety (SoCEFS) offers: B.Tech. Chemical Engineering, B.Tech. Fire and Environment, Health, Safety (Fire & EHS), and PG Diploma in Industrial Safety.

title: Programs in the School of Chemical & Industrial Sciences
content: The School of Chemical & Industrial Sciences (SoCIS) offers: B.Sc. (Hons.) Chemistry, Integrated BS-MS Pharmaceutical Science, Integrated B.Sc.-M.Sc. Chemistry, Integrated B.Sc. (H)-M.Sc. Data Science, M.Sc. Chemistry, M.Sc. Data Science, Ph.D. Chemistry, and Ph.D. Mathematics.

title: Programs in the School of Life Sciences
content: The School of Life Sciences (SoLS) offers: B.Sc. (Hons.) Biotechnology, B.Sc. (Hons.) Microbiology, M.Sc. Biotechnology, M.Sc. Microbiology, Ph.D. Biotechnology, and Ph.D. Microbiology.

title: Programs in the School of Management & Entrepreneurship
content: The School of Management & Entrepreneurship (SoM&E) offers: BBA / BBA (Hons.) General, BBA / BBA (Hons.) Business Analytics, B.Com. / B.Com. (Hons.), BBA-MBA Integrated with AI in Business, MBA (Business Analytics, Marketing, HR, Finance), and Ph.D. Management.

title: B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (part 7)
content: The B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering Program is of Four -year duration. Each year is called an academic year and is divided into two semesters. Thus, there will be a total of eight semesters. Each semester consists of fifteen weeks of teaching. The teaching learning process involves theory classes of an hour duration and practical classes of two hours duration, physical & drills training for 2 hours. The curriculum will be delivered through various methods including chalk and talk, laboratories, power point presentations, audio, video tools, E-learning / E-content, virtual laboratories, simulations, field trips/ Industry visits, seminars, workshops, projects, models, class discussions and industrial internship. Evaluation The assessment broadly comprises of Internal Assessment (Continuous Evaluation Component) and External Assessment i.e., End Semester Examination. Each course carries 100 marks for theory with 60 marks for Internal Assessment and 40 for End Semester Examination and practical course carries additional 50 marks. The internal assessment will be through MCQ, Classroom Test, Assignment, Oral Presentation and Short Projects.

title: B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering (part 8)
content: Courses The curriculum structure is based on basic requirement courses in computer science. The program consists of Fundamental Engineering courses / Core Courses / NPTEL Elective / Specialization Elective courses / Ability and Skill Enhancement Courses. For theory classes, one credit indicates one-hour lecture per week while for practical, one credit indicates two hours practical laboratory session per week. The Core Courses (CC) are all compulsory courses. There are three kinds of Elective Courses: Discipline Specific Generic Electives (DSGE), Discipline Specific Elective (DSE) and Skill Enhancement Course (SEC). In addition, there are Ability Enhancement Compulsory Courses (AECC) and Skill Enhancement Compulsory Courses (SECC). The Core Courses, Discipline Specific Electives Courses and Discipline Specific Generic Electives are of 3 or 5 Credits each. The Skill Enhancement Course, Skill Enhancement Compulsory Courses and Ability Enhancement Compulsory Courses are of 02 credits each. A student has to earn a minimum of 184 Credits to get a degree in B. Tech in Computer Science and Engineering.

content: Bachelor of Business Administration - Business Analytics | GSFC University, Vadodara Bachelor of Business Administration - Business Analytics Bachelor of Business Administration - Business Analytics About The Program Program Outcomes Program Objectives Program USPs Program Structure Course Structure Admission Process Contact Co-ordinator E-Centre About The Program Bachelor of Business Administration - Business Analytics (BBA-BA) is the process of interpreting data to help organizations make informed, strategic decisions. It involves the collection, analysis, and interpretation of large datasets from both profit and non-profit organizations. As a rapidly emerging discipline, Business Analytics has become a vital component of management science, where decision-making is largely data-driven. In view of, huge data across functional areas like marketing, finance, Production, Purchase, HR, Logistics. The complexity of data is increasing with the growth of the business and competition in the concerned sector. Therefore, Business analytics is becoming an effective tool in dealing with decision making which is complex in terms of magnitude of data.

title: Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) (part 1)
content: CBCS (Choice Based Credit System) | GSFC University, Vadodara CBCS (Choice Based Credit System) CBCS (Choice Based Credit System) It is needless to say that education play a significant role in building a nation. However, present education system lacks in creating impart on the quality of education with deficiency in confidence, and skills as it does not attend to focus on holistic development of students. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a learner centric approach with a proper education delivery mechanism so that such deficiencies can overcome. Therefore, there is a need to allow flexibility in education system. So, that students depending upon their interest can choose choice based inter-disciplinary and skilled based courses which can be possible only when Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) in its true spirit is adopted. From the Academic Year 2021-22 (Odd Semester), University is going to offer different inter-disciplinary courses under Choice Based Credit System (CBCS). Courses of 2 credits each will be offered from 1st semester to 6th semester across the University (For SoS till 4th Semester & for SoM till 5th Semester).

title: Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) (part 2)
content: Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) offers an effective learning platform for students by broadening the horizons of education by allowing students to choose their subjects of Choice & Interest. CBCS helps students to pursue courses of their choice, study at their own pace, learn extra courses, and acquire more than the required credits. A student will earn additional 4 credits (maximum) in each semester with total 12 credits for SoS, 10 credits for SoM and 24 Credits for SoT during the entire program of study. The students will have a choice of not pursuing the electives or may select one elective / two electives as per her/his areas of interest. The additional credits will be reflected in the marksheet as wells as transcript but it won't be reflected for SGPA/CGPA calculation. CBCS Course Curriculum CBCS Course Curriculum (ALL PROGRAMS)

At GSFC University, both CSE and CE share a common foundation in computing, but they differ in focus and career orientation. • Computer Science & Engineering (CSE): CSE emphasizes software development, algorithms, artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, and cybersecurity. It prepares students to design and optimize software solutions, work on emerging technologies, and handle large-scale data-driven systems. • Computer Engineering (CE): CE combines computer science with electronics and hardware engineering. Students learn about microprocessors, embedded systems, VLSI design, and hardware-software integration. It prepares students for roles that require knowledge of both computing and physical systems, such as chip design and embedded programming. • At GSFC University: CSE students gain additional exposure to AI/ML, IoT & Automation, and Cyber Security, making the program more industry-aligned with current technology needs.

CSE and IT are closely related, but they serve different purposes in the industry. • Computer Science & Engineering (CSE): Focuses on building and innovating technology itself. Students learn software engineering, AI/ML, IoT, cybersecurity, and theoretical foundations like algorithms and operating systems. CSE graduates often work in software development, AI research, data science, and security engineering . • Information Technology (IT): Primarily deals with the application of existing technologies to solve business problems. IT professionals focus on networking, databases, system administration, and managing IT infrastructure. IT graduates often work as network administrators, system analysts, or IT managers. • At GSFC University: CSE curriculum is designed with strong industry linkages and specialization tracks (AI/ML & Data Science, IoT & Automation, Cyber Security), giving students wider career opportunities compared to traditional IT programs. 3. title: PINUPS (part 1)
content: President’s Initiative for Nurturing Unlimited Potentials of Students (PINUPS) | GSFC University, Vadodara President’s Initiative for Nurturing Unlimited Potentials of Students (PINUPS) President’s Initiative for Nurturing Unlimited Potentials of Students (PINUPS) PINUPS A key mission of GSFC University is to enhance the quality of the graduating student experience. Students aim to expand their knowledge and skills throughout their academic journey, preparing for successful and fulfilling careers. In this endeavor, teachers play a crucial role by offering compassionate support, fostering an environment where students feel comfortable and encouraged to share their concerns openly, thus facilitating effective communication. GSFC University is dedicated to discover ‘Unlimited Potential’ of the students creating industry-ready, employable graduates through a holistic, student-centric approach. The concept of 'Unlimited Potential' in education captures the profound, often hidden dimensions of student development, reaching well beyond traditional categorizations. It recognizes the vast array of talents, interests, and personal traits unique to each student, ready to be discovered and nurtured. This idea underscores the expansive possibilities within every individual, going beyond the boundaries of established labels or activities.

title: PINUPS (part 2)
content: Recognizing this vision, the President of GSFC University is deeply invested in the future of the students and the institution’s role in achieving this goal. As a result, there is a pressing need for a unique initiative aimed at identifying and nurturing the top 1% of students. These high-achievers would receive tailored guidance, support, and mentoring through special programs, ensuring they stand out and make a significant impact in their future careers. Implementation: PINUPS Selection Framework Overview Phase I- Orientation: At the onset of the Academic Year 2024-2025, the PINUPS Team will initiate Orientation sessions, guiding students through the PINUPS initiative and its objectives, particularly tailored for first-year students. Phase II- Expression of Interest: Students will express their interest in PINUPS through a formal process Phase III- The committee will review the expression of interest forms submitted by students and identify those who have shown interest in showcasing their talents. The committee will conduct interviews for shortlisted students/year/program . Subsequently, students/year/program will be recommended by the committee to progress to the next round, which is the talent showcase.

title: PINUPS (part 3)
content: Phase IV- Talent Show: The talent show provides students with an opportunity to showcase their wide-ranging talents and creativity, contributing to the creation of a positive and inclusive campus atmosphere that encourages participation and appreciation for diverse forms of talent. Phase V- Personal Interview (PI): To ensure fairness and thoroughness, PINUPS 2.0 will also undergo a Personal Interview (PI) as part of the selection process. Phase VI- Formation of President's Meritorious Group (PMG): The students selected through the PINUPS process are known as the President's Meritorious Group (PMG). ~1% of the total intake will be selected based on above mentioned criteria, ensuring a diverse and well-rounded group. Phase VII- Allocating students to the Mentors: Each participating student will be paired with an internal mentor from their respective school. The role of these internal mentors will then connect them with an external mentor who specializes in their particular area of expertise.

title: PINUPS (part 4)
content: Phase VIII- Self- Assessment by the students: Students chosen for mentoring will be requested to complete a comprehensive Self-Assessment form. This form is designed to delve into various aspects, including their personality traits, goals, aspirations, and expectations from the university. This approach ensures that the mentoring process is tailored to each student's unique needs and aligns with their personal and academic growth objectives. Phase IX- Continuous Mentoring: Assigned mentors play a crucial role in offering continuous guidance and support to students throughout the academic year, nurturing both personal and professional development. Phase X- Feedback: Continuous improvement is integral to the PINUPS initiative, with a commitment to refining and enhancing its success based on valuable feedback garnered from the previous year. This iterative refinement process ensures that the program evolves and adapts to better meet the needs of the students and align with its overarching goals. Community Service: NCC promotes a sense of social responsibility by engaging in various community development and social service activities. National Integration: NCC aims to foster a sense of unity and integration among the diverse cultures, religions, languages, and regions of India. Adventure and Sports: NCC encourages adventure activities and sports to promote physical fitness, courage, and team spirit among the cadets. Structure of NCC The NCC is organized into different directorates covering all states and union territories of India. The structure includes Senior Division (for college and university students) and Junior Division (for school students). The cadets are grouped into Army, Navy, and Air Wing based on their interests and career goals.

National Events: NCC cadets participate in Republic Day Parade, Prime Minister’s Rally, and other national and state-level events, showcasing their skills and discipline. The NCC plays a vital role in shaping the youth of India into responsible citizens who are committed to the service of the nation. It acts as a platform for holistic development, fostering a sense of patriotism and unity among the youth.
